newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah falls at close on spillover.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah falls at close on spillover.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah weakened against the dollar on Thursday as regional nervousness continued to spill over into the currency, dealers said.
Spot rupiah ended at 2,610/20 at 0910 GMT in Jakarta. The rupiah opened at 2,575/85 but fell to a low of 2,625 in the morning following a currency slump in the region.
"Sentiment remains bearish and people are very cautious with the on-going currency woes in the region," one dealer said.
Another dealer said a report by UBS Research that the rupiah was likely to come under further pressure as the corporate sector was facing debt problems also weakened the currency.

"There is evidence that more Indonesian corporates are facing difficulties in rolling over their maturing foreign liabilities," the report said, pointing to higher risk premiums and possibly lower credit limits because of falling investor confidence in nations with large current account deficits.
"As a result, more Indonesian corporates will have to buy rupiah and convert into foreign currency domestically."
"Unless supported by strong intervention from Bank Indonesia, this will add pressure to the rupiah."
On Monday, the rupiah plunged to a historic low of 2,665 to the dollar but recovered slightly on central bank intervention.

UBS said the rupiah weakness was triggered by an attack on the baht because of the perception that Thailand's rigid exchange rate regime was inconsistent with sharply dropping economic activity and high domestic interest rates.
Indonesia has a much more flexible foreign exchange system, robust economic activity and ample liquidity in the financial system, it added.
Dealers were mixed whether the sporadic uptrend of the rupiah at midday was attributable to central bank intervention or to stop-loss selling of dollars in late morning.
One U.S. bank dealer said earlier stop-loss was triggered at the 2,590 level after local operators were forced to unload dollars to obtain rupiah due to rising swap rates.
But another dealer said there was talk of central bank checking prices and possible intervention.

Dealers said the central bank move to raise overnight rates by one percentage point and the absence of short-term securities (SBPUs) purchases by Bank Indonesia helped drain excess supply of short-term liquidity.
The central bank did not buy any SBPUs on Thursday.
"It's a smart move from the central bank to contain short-term liquidity without shocking the market. This will help prevent dollar buying with cheap rupiah," one Japanese bank dealer said.
The central bank raised its interest rates for overnight bilateral papers by one percentage point to 14.0 percent on Thursday while keeping other rates unchanged.
Dealers said the move pushed short-dated swaps up, with overnight swap rising to 0.30/0.35 from -0.2/par and tom/next to 0.4/0.6 from -0.7 points.
Overnight rupiah ended at 14.0 percent.
One-month swap was at 19.0/22.0, two at 42.0/50.0, three at 63.0/71.0 and six at 122.0/127.0 points.
Dealers said the tone on the swap market remained biddish.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,378/2,682 but raised the conversion band to 2,566/2,614 on Thursday from 2,549/2,597 on Wednesday.
